props.gloss_en: there is no difference between Shabbat and Yom Kippur except that this one's deliberate violation is [punished] at the hand of man and that one's with karet
it follows that with regard to payments, this one and that one are equal
whose is the mishna? It is R' Nechunya ben HaKana's

R' Nechunya ben HaKana would make Yom Kippur like Shabbat for payments: as on Shabbat one is liable with his life and exempt from payment, so on Yom Kippur one is liable with his life and exempt from payment
all those liable to karet who were flogged are exempted from their karet
as it is said, 'and your brother be degraded before your eyes' (Deut 25:3): once he was flogged he is as your brother
R' Yochanan: R' Chananya ben Gamliel's colleagues disagree with him
bei Rav: we have learned it -- the mishna contrasts Shabbat (at the hand of man) with Yom Kippur (karet); were [R' Chananya ben Gamliel's ruling] so, both would be at the hand of man
Rav Nachman: whose is this [mishna]? It is R' Yitzchak's
there are no lashes for those liable to karet
R' Yitzchak: all those liable to karet were included in the general rule; why was karet for one's sister singled out? to sentence her to karet and not to lashes
Rav Ashi: even if you say [the mishna is] the Rabbis' -- [it means] this one's primary deliberate violation is at the hand of man, and that one's primary deliberate violation is with karet

supports.gloss_en: the mishna names punishment as the ONLY difference, so in payments the two are alike (marker: the bare הא; see header)
דתניא: R' Nechunya ben HaKana makes Yom Kippur like Shabbat for payments -- the equality the mishna implies
דתניא, רבי יצחק אומר: karet for one's sister was singled out to sentence her to karet and not to lashes

תנינא: the mishna sets Yom Kippur's karet against Shabbat's punishment at the hand of man; if lashes (at the hand of man) exempted from karet, both would be at the hand of man -- so the mishna's tanna disagrees with R' Chananya ben Gamliel

deflected_by.gloss_en: הא מני -- רבי יצחק היא, דאמר מלקות בחייבי כריתות ליכא: the mishna is R' Yitzchak's, for whom there are no lashes where there is karet, so it says nothing about whether lashes exempt from karet
אפילו תימא רבנן: זה עיקר זדונו בידי אדם וזה עיקר זדונו בהיכרת -- even on the Rabbis' view the mishna speaks of each day's PRIMARY punishment, so it is no proof against R' Chananya ben Gamliel
